engine.name: codex review panel (workflow engine)
engine.shape: one lens-deriver agent (sol/medium) + one lens-free native sweep + N diff-derived scalpel native reviews (sol/xhigh) + one binding verifier agent (sol/high)

baseline.engine: single codex review through review-engine.sh, gpt-5.6-sol xhigh (production path)
baseline.why_this_one: the most recent codex run scored on the current post-#36 fixtures (truth denominator 20); the earlier baseline-r1/r2 pair was scored against the pre-maintenance fixtures

bar.rule: seeded recall >= baseline seeded recall AND total seeded-set FP <= baseline FP + 1

totals.verdict: PASS — recall 17/17 = baseline 17/17; FP 1 vs baseline 0 (+1, the maximum the bar allows)

adjudication.rules_applied: mechanism match against each case's truth.json (file+line overlap is evidence, mechanism is the criterion); one finding matches at most one truth entry; a flagged bait is an FP by construction; a finding that surfaces a genuine unseeded defect is credited to neither side and excluded from FP (X1 README).

Not a bait — bait (2) only claims the find rewrite preserves the glob's set, and it does.

sensitivity.note: the PASS depends on the exclusions above; the strictest reading (counting every non-truth finding as an FP) puts the panel at FP 5 and the baseline codex r3 at FP 2, so the panel would fail. The symmetric reading — the X1 rule as written, applied to both engines' unseeded candidates alike — is the one scored here.

mechanics.coverage: 22 finder lanes across 5 cases, all status=ok — zero dead workers, zero extraction failures
mechanics.clean_sentinel: NOT EXERCISED — every one of the 22 finders returned at least two parsed findings, so no lane ever had to render a clean review. The sentinel contract remains unvalidated live in its positive direction; the negative direction (a clean-looking prose render mis-read as a failure) did not occur either.
mechanics.render_format: every finder rendered `- [P#] Title — path:line[-line]` heads with no orphan tags; extraction parsed 97 stubs total with zero partial-drift rejections
